jobs.title: Federal Mine Remediation Lead
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking a Federal
Mine Remediation Lead
to be based out of any of our locations in the western United States (AZ, CA, CO, MT, NM, NV, OR, UT). This is a full-time role.

This is an exciting growth focused opportunity to build and lead a Mine remediation group. The person in this position will support business development, project execution and have the ability to grow and lead a Mine Remediation practice. We are seeking a leader with major project delivery experience and proven ability to build and lead technical teams in implementing Mine remediation projects, specifically under CERCLA. Preferential consideration will be given to experience on US Federal projects and strong regulatory connections.

As an experienced professional in Mine remediation, you will bring specific technical expertise, sophisticated regulatory understanding, leadership skills, and an entrepreneurial spirit along with a keen interest in evolving and growing the business and mentoring staff. Your demonstrated commitment to safety along with a strong operational understanding of safety risks in mining environments, and ability to mentor employees to support a safe work culture will supplement AECOM’s existing safety culture.

Responsibilities will include:

Working closely with AECOM personnel in United States and Canada to develop and implement Mine remedial solutions for clients in the public and private sector that meet regulatory requirements and protect human health and the environment.
Collaboration with, and coordination of, diverse technical teams including hydrologists, hydrogeologists, geochemists, risk assessors, environmental engineers, geotechnical engineers, civil engineers, water treatment specialists, biologists, revegetation, costing specialists, etc. to develop remedial solutions that meet technical and regulatory requirements.
Reviewing technical work plans and cost estimates; interpreting data; conducting remediation/closure technology evaluations and feasibility studies.
Technical and financial management of projects to meet commitments on budget, quality and schedule.
Development of proposals, project teams and cost estimates.
Delivery of projects, and technical review of reports for regulatory submission (e.g., studies, remediation and closure plans, permit applications, management plans).
Periodically attending site visits to proposed, operating or closed mines in support of client relationship building, proposal development and project delivery.
Business-development activities, including building and maintaining existing and new client relationships, tracking marketing leads and project opportunities, developing proposals and presentations, networking, attending conferences and sharing AECOM’s capabilities with existing and potential clients.
Stakeholder communications, including regulatory communications and client advocacy.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in relevant engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Environmental etc.) or science (geology, hydrogeology, environmental etc.) disciplines +8 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or 20+ years of experience
People management experience
Mine remediation experience under CERCLA framework
Proficient technical writing experience for investigation and design reports and regulatory document submissions
Proficient proposals preparation and cost development experience for Mine remediation projects
Experience with US Federal projects, specifically with US Army Corps of Engineers, US Environmental Project Agency, US Department of Interior

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $160000 to $210000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Associate Consultant, Air Quality
jobs.description:
Company Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Inviting bright minds

Do you want to develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and creative culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world.

Ramboll is seeking an Air Quality Associate to join the firm’s offices in Los Angeles or Irvine, California, or Phoenix, Arizona. If you are detail-oriented, self-motivated and enjoy thinking “outside-of-the-box,” please apply! If you can work in a team, apply analytical skills, and are looking to get your hands dirty (literally and figuratively), then you may find Ramboll to be an ideal place to start your career.

Job Description

You will join our Environment & Health
department

As our new Entry Level Air Quality Consultant you will be part of the Air & Climate Service Line within Ramboll’s Environment & Health Division. This group consists of like-minded individuals who are passionate about air and climate issues and assisting Ramboll’s clients with their most challenging problems. The Air & Climate team consults with clients across various industries on a range of topics, including but not limited to emissions estimation, air dispersion modeling, human health risk assessment, climate change, permitting, and compliance.

Your key tasks and responsibilities will be:

Preparing emissions calculations
Conducting air quality reviews of emissions reduction or control
Assisting in preparing major and minor source permit applications and environmental impact reports
Critically reviewing and interpreting local, state, and federal environmental regulations

Qualifications

Your starting point for constant growth

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

B.S. or M.S. in Chemical, Mechanical, Civil, or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Atmospheric Science, or a science degree with air quality course work
Strong computing skills including high level use of spreadsheets and word processing
Strong written/verbal communication, problem-solving and organization skills
Ability to understand and interpret environmental regulations
Database and GIS skills are preferred but not required

Additional Information

Welcome to our Environment & Health division

Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase live ability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $64,404 to $80,505 yearly. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

How To Apply

Apply online. Attach your CV, cover letter and relevant documents showcasing why you are the right fit for the role, and when you are available to start. We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.title: Senior Agrochemical Regulatory Affairs Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

Inviting bright minds

Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world. Ramboll Health Science Spearhead has approx. 360 bright minds globally and you can become one of them in our Australia team contributing to our continued success.

You will join our Environment and Health Business Unit

As our new Senior Consultant, you will have experience and be a subject matter expert in Agrochemical regulations in Australia (APVMA) and New Zealand (EPA and ACVM). You will bring the ability to organize, coordinate and communicate across an interdisciplinary team, engaging externally with technical professionals, and regulatory agencies. You will provide strategic expertise and support the preparation of regulatory submissions for a variety of agrochemical related products in the region. A strong customer service ethic and ability to multitask is vital for this role. You will present a positive “can-do” attitude and be a self-starter within a team of dedicated professionals.

This is a unique opportunity to have a role within the Ramboll Health Science Spearhead to help drive the growth of the agrochemical consulting business in Australia, working with our international team of regulatory and technical experts, while advancing your skills and consulting career. Reporting to the Principal, Health Sciences in Australia your role would be based at one of Ramboll’s Australian Offices.

Your key tasks and responsibility will be:

Support the execution of Product Stewardship and Safety projects with a focus on Australian and New Zealand plant protection registrations
Act as project manager for interdisciplinary agrochemical regulatory projects
Responsible for strategic guidance and translating complex scientific information into regulator-ready submissions.
Advise clients on existing as well as upcoming regulatory obligations (in the fields of environmental, health & safety-related topics)
Developing strategies, market analysis and helping to expand and drive the growth of Ramboll’s agrochemical business in the region.
Active in business development, meeting clients and attending appropriate conferences and seminars to increase Ramboll’s visibility in the region.

Your starting point for constant growth

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional developments so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

Ability to provide strategic advice and determine practical compliance solutions to meet our clients’ commercial aims for their agricultural related products.
Experience leading multi-faceted teams on projects, producing a high-quality work product, on time and within budget
Ability to guide clients through registrations, variations, and label/claims strategies, helping to prepare compliance advice, application dossiers and data-gap analyses.
Staying current with changes in regulatory landscape affecting Ramboll’s clients and maintaining contacts and relationships with regulatory authorities.
Proficiency assessing the impact of new regional regulations on the business and participates in actions to assist our clients in dealing with the implementation of these new regulations.
Strong team player and customer-oriented approach.

Qualifications

Desired skills/experience

A minimum of 7 years’ industry or consulting experience with plant protection product registration in Australia and New Zealand
Scientific background preferably with a degree or higher in agriculture, veterinary medicine, chemistry, biology or a related discipline
Ability to handle multiple tasks and work streams in a fast-paced environment while maintaining outstanding attention to detail and quality of deliverables
Experience/comfort with working in a virtual team with stakeholders across geographies
Ability to support internal and external clients with both technical and strategic consulting services
Experience in business development would be advantageous
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good presentation skills and business sense
Demonstrated problem-solving skills
Possess a drive and personal initiative to keep learning and improving in the chosen field.

Additional Information

Welcome to our Environment & Health division

Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase livability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll has close to 500 experts working across more than 10 offices in Asia Pacific. We are present in Australia, China, Hong Kong SAR, Malaysia, India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore. Our experts are applying their passion to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions in markets as diverse as Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy and Architecture &, Landscape. Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a people company. We invite you to contribute to a sustainable future working in an open, collaborative and empowering culture.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in Asia Pacific has close to 500 people working across ten offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, and Architecture & Landscape.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

Collaboration with, and coordination of, diverse technical teams including hydrologists, hydrogeologists, geochemists, risk assessors, environmental engineers, geotechnical engineers, civil engineers, water treatment specialists, biologists, revegetation, costing specialists, etc. to develop remedial solutions that meet technical and regulatory requirements.
Reviewing technical work plans and cost estimates; interpreting data; conducting remediation/closure technology evaluations and feasibility studies.
Technical and financial management of projects to meet commitments on budget, quality and schedule.
Development of proposals, project teams and cost estimates.
Delivery of projects, and technical review of reports for regulatory submission (e.g., studies, remediation and closure plans, permit applications, management plans).
Periodically attending site visits to proposed, operating or closed mines in support of client relationship building, proposal development and project delivery.
Business-development activities, including building and maintaining existing and new client relationships, tracking marketing leads and project opportunities, developing proposals and presentations, networking, attending conferences and sharing AECOM’s capabilities with existing and potential clients.
Stakeholder communications, including regulatory communications and client advocacy

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in relevant engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Environmental etc.) or science (geology, hydrogeology, environmental etc.) disciplines +10 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education, including 2 years of leadership
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or 20+ years of experience
People management experience
Experience managing complex environmental consulting or Engineering, Procurement, and Construction Management (EPCM) projects
Experience with remediation under CERCLA and RCRA frameworks
Proficient technical writing experience for investigation and design reports and regulatory document submissions
Proficient proposals preparation and cost development experience for Mine remediation projects
Some experience with NEPA, CWA, and NPDES permitting
Experience working on projects for mining companies
Experience with US Federal projects, specifically with US Army Corps of Engineers, US Environmental Project Agency, US Department of Interior

Additional Information

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $190000 to $230000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

new_jobs.title: Senior Agrochemical Regulatory Affairs Consultant
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Inviting bright minds

Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world. Ramboll Health Science Spearhead has approx. 360 bright minds globally and you can become one of them in our Australia team contributing to our continued success.

You will join our Environment and Health Business Unit

As our new Senior Consultant, you will have experience and be a subject matter expert in Agrochemical regulations in Australia (APVMA) and New Zealand (EPA and ACVM). You will bring the ability to organize, coordinate and communicate across an interdisciplinary team, engaging externally with technical professionals, and regulatory agencies. You will provide strategic expertise and support the preparation of regulatory submissions for a variety of agrochemical related products in the region. A strong customer service ethic and ability to multitask is vital for this role. You will present a positive “can-do” attitude and be a self-starter within a team of dedicated professionals.

This is a unique opportunity to have a role within the Ramboll Health Science Spearhead to help drive the growth of the agrochemical consulting business in Australia, working with our international team of regulatory and technical experts, while advancing your skills and consulting career. Reporting to the Principal, Health Sciences in Australia your role would be based at one of Ramboll’s Australian Offices.

Your key tasks and responsibility will be:

Support the execution of Product Stewardship and Safety projects with a focus on Australian and New Zealand plant protection registrations
Act as project manager for interdisciplinary agrochemical regulatory projects
Responsible for strategic guidance and translating complex scientific information into regulator-ready submissions.
Advise clients on existing as well as upcoming regulatory obligations (in the fields of environmental, health & safety-related topics)
Developing strategies, market analysis and helping to expand and drive the growth of Ramboll’s agrochemical business in the region.
Active in business development, meeting clients and attending appropriate conferences and seminars to increase Ramboll’s visibility in the region.

Your starting point for constant growth

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional developments so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

Ability to provide strategic advice and determine practical compliance solutions to meet our clients’ commercial aims for their agricultural related products.
Experience leading multi-faceted teams on projects, producing a high-quality work product, on time and within budget
Ability to guide clients through registrations, variations, and label/claims strategies, helping to prepare compliance advice, application dossiers and data-gap analyses.
Staying current with changes in regulatory landscape affecting Ramboll’s clients and maintaining contacts and relationships with regulatory authorities.
Proficiency assessing the impact of new regional regulations on the business and participates in actions to assist our clients in dealing with the implementation of these new regulations.
Strong team player and customer-oriented approach.

Qualifications

Desired skills/experience

A minimum of 7 years’ industry or consulting experience with plant protection product registration in Australia and New Zealand
Scientific background preferably with a degree or higher in agriculture, veterinary medicine, chemistry, biology or a related discipline
Ability to handle multiple tasks and work streams in a fast-paced environment while maintaining outstanding attention to detail and quality of deliverables
Experience/comfort with working in a virtual team with stakeholders across geographies
Ability to support internal and external clients with both technical and strategic consulting services
Experience in business development would be advantageous
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good presentation skills and business sense
Demonstrated problem-solving skills
Possess a drive and personal initiative to keep learning and improving in the chosen field.

Additional Information

Welcome to our Environment & Health division

Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase livability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll has close to 500 experts working across more than 10 offices in Asia Pacific. We are present in Australia, China, Hong Kong SAR, Malaysia, India, Japan, South Korea and Singapore. Our experts are applying their passion to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions in markets as diverse as Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy and Architecture &, Landscape. Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a people company. We invite you to contribute to a sustainable future working in an open, collaborative and empowering culture.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in Asia Pacific

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in Asia Pacific has close to 500 people working across ten offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, and Architecture & Landscape.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.
